sources.title: Trump, sobre la renuncia de Huang (Nvidia): “Solo Tim Cook puede sustituirle”
sources.text: Al presidente Donald Trump no le ha salido bien la quiniela sobre el futuro de Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia. “Creo que saldrá bien parado”, afirmó el mandatario tras hablar con el directivo y confirmar que el FBI estaba investigando el affaire que había mantenido con una mujer acusada de ser una espía china. 48 horas después, el mandamás de la multinacional de Santa Clara ha presentado su renuncia, por la presión de la junta, se que se planteaba su despido tras conocerse una segunda relación extramatrimonial, en esta ocasión, con una empleada de la empresa. La compañía dependía mucho del liderazgo hiper personalista de Huang y no había un plan a corto plazo para sustituirlo. Será la directora financiera la que tomará el rol de manera interina mientras se buscan opciones tanto dentro como fuera de la casa. Pues bien, Trump no ha dudado en afirmar públicamente quién debería ser el nuevo CEO de Nvidia. “Solo Tim Cook puede hacerlo”, ha asegurado en sus redes sociales el mandatario. “Una leyenda sustituye a una leyenda”, ha aseverado el mandatario. Donald Trump mantenía una relación cercana con el CEO saliente de Nvidia. Y en varias ocasiones ha expresado su admiración con Tim Cook, actualmente presidente de Apple, tras ceder el bastón de mando y puesto de director ejecutivo a John Ternus el pasado 1 de septiembre después de 15 años al frente de la compañía de Cupertino. sources.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang’s successor
sources.text: In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple. Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company , but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China. Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday , suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs. Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess. “Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does . sources.title: Trump pide a Tim Cook como CEO de NVIDIA tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang: «Una leyenda por otra leyenda»
sources.text: La renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA es, sin dudas, el tema del día . El escándalo por infidelidades le ha costado al empresario el puesto que ostentó durante los últimos 33 años , y el asunto promete seguir dando que hablar por bastante tiempo. Lo más curioso es que todos tienen una opinión sobre el tema y hasta Donald Trump ha propuesto a un reemplazante de alto perfil: Tim Cook . En las horas posteriores a la salida de Jensen Huang, Trump usó su perfil en Truth Social para postular a Cook como próximo CEO de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con el presidente de Estados Unidos, el exCEO de Apple es la única persona que tiene lo necesario para hacerse cargo de un rol tan complejo. A sabiendas de cómo piensa y actúa Donald Trump, no quedan dudas de que el mandatario estadounidense habla en serio. Claro que hoy parece improbable que Tim Cook esté dispuesto a asumir un rol tan notorio fuera de Apple, en especial por lo repentino y desastroso del desenlace de Jensen Huang. "Ahora que el CEO de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, quien ha hecho un trabajo fantástico, ha renunciado, solo hay un hombre capaz de tomar su lugar: Tim Cook, de Apple. ¡Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda! Presidente Donald J. Trump", publicó el presidente de Estados Unidos. Más allá de las virtudes de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook para conducir durante gran cantidad de años (y con gran éxito) a sus respectivas empresas, Trump no ofrece detalles de por qué el exjefe de Apple debería reemplazar a su antiguo colega en NVIDIA. Tal vez solo sea porque Cook ha sabido congraciarse con el presidente estadounidense durante sus mandatos, tal y como lo hizo Huang en su momento. Sea como sea, todavía no se sabe quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. Colette Kress , la jefa de finanzas de NVIDIA, fungirá de CEO interina hasta que se designe a un nuevo responsable del cargo. La junta del gigante verde anunció la puesta en marcha de un proceso de búsqueda de nuevo consejero delegado, para la cual analizará a candidatos internos y externos. Asimismo, se ha designado a Harvey C. Jones como presidente del board , el primero en ocupar ese rol en la historia de la compañía. ¿Tiene posibilidades Tim Cook de ser el próximo CEO de NVIDIA? Hasta hace menos de 15 días, era inaudito pensar en dicha empresa sin Jensen Huang como jefe, pero ya hemos visto que los imposibles no existen y que no se puede descartar nada. Dicho esto, Cook se encuentra extremadamente cómodo en su nuevo rol como presidente ejecutivo de Apple. Además, no es un directivo enfocado en producto como sí lo fue Jensen Huang ; algo que podría no importar en cualquier otra empresa, pero que ha sido crucial para el crecimiento de NVIDIA bajo el comando de un único CEO en sus 33 años de vida. Ya veremos qué novedades surgen en tal sentido.

stories.title: Nvidia staff wait 6 days for an all-hands after Jensen Huang’s exit. PR experts warn employees need answers sooner
stories.summary: “Even if she didn't have every single aspect 100% sorted out at that moment, it's too long to wait,” a communications executive told Fortune.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Nvidia staff wait 6 days for an all-hands after Jensen Huang’s exit. PR experts warn employees need answers sooner
sources.text: On Thursday, Nvidia announced CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation , effective immediately, following his admission to having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times has also reported that he had an affair with another Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care. Neither Nvidia nor Powell has publicly addressed that report. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO , and one of her first moves was addressing employees. But the company won’t hold an all-hands meeting until Nov. 18, six days after Thursday’s announcement, and several communications experts told Fortune that’s too long to leave a shaken workforce waiting. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, having previously held senior finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft . She ranked No. 49 on the 2026 Fortune Most Powerful Women list . She takes over a company whose market value topped $5 trillion at its peak. Nvidia, No. 16 on the 2026 Fortune 500, was the first company on the list to pass $4 trillion . It has since dropped below that mark after news of Huang’s affairs and his resignation. Nvidia could also be drawn into multiple Justice Department investigations, including an antitrust probe aimed at the chipmaker itself and two separate inquiries into Megaspeed and Supermicro that center on Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy, Semafor reported , citing two administration officials. Semafor reported no sign the DOJ currently intends to pursue criminal charges against Nvidia or Huang. Fortune has reported on why Nvidia can’t shake China smuggling allegations . Some employees have voiced their shock publicly. “Jensen Huang rescued me from probably living in debt the rest of my life … I’ve never spoken to him, and only passed by him in HQ once,” one X user who identifies themself as an Nvidia employee wrote in a post on Thursday. “His personal life is frankly none of my business. But as a leader, I have yet to meet a better one.” “Ousting him is financial suicide, and I can only assume there is a hidden ulterior motive because I can’t fathom any other reason for destroying the company’s value,” the Nvidia employee continued. Prominent business leaders, including billionaires Bill Ackman and Elon Musk, have also defended Huang online. “@JensenHuang is human. And he is an incredible human. Even incredible humans make mistakes,” Ackman posted on X on Sunday. “Onward.” Musk responded “I agree” to a post from Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire arguing “Jensen is one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation … he did something incredibly dumb … it was bad for America … but my guess is there was no bad intention … [and] two mistakes don’t make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to Fortune ‘s request for comment. The timing comes from a message sent to Nvidia employees that has since circulated publicly: “You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a meeting on November 18 at 9 am PT.” “We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us,” the message continued. “So let’s move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company.” The meeting also lands the day after Nvidia reports third-quarter results on Nov. 17 , meaning Wall Street will hear from the company’s new leadership before employees get a company-wide forum. Annie Scranton, founder and CEO of Pace Public Relations, told Fortune that while Kress gets points for how quickly the message went out and its overall tone, the timing of the all-hands meeting isn’t great. “The problem lies with her giving a specific day that is nearly a week away for the all-hands,” Scranton said. “She should have just stopped after the line referencing that employees will hear more from leadership in the coming days. “‘Coming days’ to me does not mean six days away,” she continued. Scranton said that, “Understanding that they have a ton to work out,” Kress should have pushed to do the meeting on Monday, working through the weekend to figure out messaging and next steps. “Even if she didn’t have every single aspect 100% sorted out at that moment, it’s too long to wait,” she added. “It gives employees too much time to stew, talk, get upset, and have morale and their stock plummet even more than it already has.” Amy Cuthbertson, founder of ACA PR , also would’ve favored an earlier, live briefing in which staff could have heard from Kress and raised their concerns sooner, she told Fortune . “Managers also need to be given clear guidance so they can support their teams and be in a position to answer their questions consistently,” Cuthbertson said. On what to expect from Kress, Cuthbertson said the interim CEO should avoid speculating about the investigation or promising answers she’s not in a position to give. “That said, she can still explain what is known and what remains to be determined,” Cuthbertson said. “She can also explain to staff how they will be kept updated.” To be sure, Johan Konst, founder of tech PR agency EUSA PR , said Kress “struck the right tone” by thanking employees and acknowledging the difficulty of the situation, adding he thinks six days for a company-wide meeting is “reasonable.” But “it’s too long for employees to wait to ask their first question,” he said. “I would invite questions today and answer the most pressing ones tomorrow.”

sources.title: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO just got harder after Jensen Huang’s dramatic exit as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Anthropic is about to embark on one of the most hotly anticipated IPOs in history. After a dramatic turn of events, it will now be doing so a week after the industry lost one of its most powerful figures and best salesmen. Nvidia’s longtime CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang resigned from the company on Thursday following reports alleging he had engaged in two extramarital affairs: one with a customer suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese intelligence asset and another with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. The timing has thrown new pressure on Anthropic’s listing, which was already seen as a stress test for investors’ appetite for AI. The AI lab is expected to list on Wednesday or Thursday next week, days after Nvidia reports quarterly earnings—the company’s first-ever without Huang at the helm. Nvidia is a close partner of Anthropic and intimately involved in the lab’s upcoming IPO. According to Anthropic’s filings, the chipmaker has agreed to buy about $10 billion of shares in a $26 billion private placement alongside the IPO. The two companies are also closely tied commercially, with Anthropic committing to tens of billions of dollars to secure access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips. Investors and analysts told Fortune that while they don’t expect the Nvidia shock to affect Anthropic’s core business, it could cause problems for the broader AI story. Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners and one of the few on Wall Street with a sell rating on Nvidia’s stock, doesn’t expect Huang’s exit to derail the deal. “They’re going to go public right in the face of Nvidia’s earnings call, and I don’t think that derails it,” he said. “It’s such a massive IPO and there’s so many people behind it now that they don’t pull the IPO.” The bigger risk, he said, comes once Anthropic is a public company. Speaking shortly before Huang’s departure but after reports that he was likely to be leaving the company, Goldberg warned that turmoil at Nvidia, including the loss of its CEO, would create a headwind for Anthropic when it reports its first quarterly results. “At the very least it will create this narrative of, ‘Can the AI narrative maintain? Can we keep doing this?’” he said. “They’ll get much tougher questions.” Karl Alomar, a partner at venture firm M13, agreed that Anthropic’s fundamentals haven’t changed. “From where I stand, Anthropic is still in as good, as strong a position as it was before this news came out,” he said. “Anthropic’s numbers are fantastic, and they’ve clearly shown that they have excess capacity for what they need. They haven’t spent that much money.” Anthropic is also less dependent on Nvidia than some of its rivals, running some models on Google’s TPUs, Amazon’s Trainium chips, and AMD’s GPUs, as well as Nvidia’s hardware. Anthropic has also reportedly been exploring building its own chips. “Nvidia has committed to invest $10 billion in the Anthropic IPO. That will likely still happen when the IPO eventually happens,” said Francine McKenna, an accountant and investigative journalist who has taught at the Wharton School. “But anyone who was looking at Nvidia to bail out CoreWeave if needed should probably look elsewhere.” However, the recent trouble at Nvidia and questions surrounding the CEO’s judgement could spill over into more scrutiny for its partners, according to Jason Schloetzer, an associate professor at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business. He said he expected there to be “much closer scrutiny of [Anthropic’s] ties to Nvidia and customers associated with Nvidia.” For Silicon Valley, Anthropic and competitor OpenAI have needed so much capital that almost every venture capital firm in town owns a piece of them—making them the private market equivalent of an index fund. That makes Anthropic’s expected IPO next week a high-stakes liquidity event—not only for the more than 400 backers of Anthropic, but for the AI boom as a whole. There’s a broad sense that if Anthropic succeeds, the AI boom has far more runway. If it flops or pushes back indefinitely, it would be an unequivocal negative signal that the AI bubble is heading towards a pop. It may not be a bust. Indeed, at least one venture capitalist sees a clear upside for Anthropic. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has long pushed for tighter controls on chip exports to China, putting him at odds with Huang. The AI lab has similarly clashed with Huang on AI regulation, with Huang particularly keen to avoid any licensing requirements that would make it more difficult for customers to adopt open-source AI models. “If anything, I think Anthropic is a beneficiary here,” said the investor, who asked not to be named given the situation’s sensitivity and their investments across AI. “They weren’t that close to Jensen…They’re building their own chip, and so the supply chain considerations that get freed up are good for Anthropic.”

sources.title: ‘A dark day for Nvidia’: Here’s what analysts have been saying about Jensen Huang’s departure
sources.text: Nvidia investors are preparing for a future without Jensen Huang after the CEO's resignation was announced on Thursday. Markets were on tenterhooks ahead of the decision amid reports that the chip giant's board had convened to discuss his future with the company. By the time of the announcement, at least six analysts had downgraded the stock between Wednesday night and Thursday morning. The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had engaged in a second extramarital affair with an employee. The CEO was already under scrutiny after Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy. Nvidia announced on Thursday morning that, following a board meeting, Huang would step down after more than 30 years at the company's helm. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Those downgrading the stock included longtime Nvidia bull Ben Reitzes of Melius Research. Nvidia shares were seen down more than 12% shortly after the open on Wall Street, bringing losses for the last month close to 25%. Here's what analysts and investors are saying about the company and the stock. Reitzes changed his rating for Nvidia to hold from buy. His price target is now $185 — down from $315 — is 6% above the level at which shares last closed. "We thought we had experience, but nothing prepares you for what has happened at Nvidia over the last few weeks - and especially since Saturday. The only situation remotely close to this we can recall was HP in 2010. Waiting to see what that Board would do (and who they would hire) that time didn't work out. It was really cheap, too, at ~9x EPS right after its initial swoon. Nvidia is a much stronger, more important company, but its market moves far faster, and this story touches geopolitical flashpoints. In this unique crisis, we have decided (reluctantly) to step aside on Nvidia (now a Hold) after recommending it since we launched our AI platform coverage universe in July 2023," he said. Analyst Mark Lipacis downgraded Nvidia to in line from outperform. He also lowered his price target on shares to $186 from $465, implying 7% upside from Wednesday's close. "The Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia's Board was 'preparing to oust' its CEO after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The NY Times reported that Nvidia's Board hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead an investigation into the matter. While Nvidia's Board said that it 'has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,' we believe that the investigation will take time and we expect NVDA's P/E multiple will continue to compress consistent with our 'Late-Innings of the Semi Cycle' thesis, especially since Nvidia has no obvious succession plan or number 2 operational executive," he said. William Blair's Sebastien Naji downgraded Nvidia to market perform from outperform. "After a head-spinning week of news and allegations around CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to remove him, according to the Wall Street Journal. The full story will take time to emerge and may require several investigations, including the board's own independent probe and a requested U.S. House briefing. What is already clear is that Huang's likely departure and heightened scrutiny of the company will be a significant overhang on NVDA shares in the near term. Meanwhile, the potential for a slower AI buildout and more intense competition from other chipmakers will only add to execution risk...governance and regulatory pressure, the potential for more serious fallout, and a sudden change in management are likely to muddle both execution and sentiment. As a result, we are downgrading NVDA to Market Perform and will wait for the dust to settle before reassessing," he said. Analyst Rick Schafer downgraded the AI stock to perform from outperform. "We are downgrading shares of NVDA and removing our price target following reports (WSJ, NYT) of founding CEO Jensen Huang's imminent departure amidst allegations of a 2nd extramarital affair. Credible media reports circulated Wednesday evening that NVDA's board is preparing to part ways with Huang following a widely reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy compounded by new allegations of a relationship with an NVDA executive. This 'one-two' punch appears to have forced the board's hand...While we see upside to the F3Q (Oct.) print and F4Q (Jan.) outlook, we expect fundamentals to take a backseat near term. The departure of Mr. Huang could, in our view, translate to a lingering share overhang," he said. Analyst Stacy Rasgon slashed his price target from $400 and downgraded the stock from market outperform. "So now what? On the positive, the fundamentals of the business (if not the leadership) are clearly still intact with numbers that remain massive (and probably still headed higher). We don't think the company should have huge issues operating while engaged in a search for new leadership. And (of course) the shares are almost absurdly cheap (and getting cheaper as we speak); clearly there is a lot of bad news getting priced in here," he said. "On the other hand, we find it hard to advocate stepping in here in size as there will no doubt be more allegations to come (there is a trope that says if you find two ants in your kitchen the best estimate of the total number of ants in your kitchen is not two...), both from internal issues as well as headlines related to the business, new governmental investigations etc. Adding on the new variable of who will take the reins (internal? external?) and anything else they may or may not uncover creates additional uncertainty (and we can't even begin to speculate as to who they might find to fill Jensen's shoes)," he added. Analyst John Vinh downgraded the stock from overweight. "We believe Huang's departure represents a material increase in strategic, organizational, and execution risk that warrants a higher risk

sources.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
sources.text: Michael Dell described Jensen Huang as a "visionary of the AI age." Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges said a photo with the Nvidia CEO produced more media coverage for his company than its iPhone launch. During the keynote of his annual Dreamforce conference, Salesforce's Marc Benioff said, "Jensen, we're all following you, bro," as the two paced through the audience. Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation His fame extended way beyond tech. In May, Huang joined President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping . Three months later, Huang gathered six of the biggest names at the Nasdaq to announce on CNBC a proposed $500 billion artificial intelligence buildout plan, cementing his central role at the intersection of Wall Street and Silicon Valley. As Nvidia became the first company to rip past a $5 trillion market cap, bending the laws of physics with its advanced graphics processing units and pushing the AI boom to seemingly endless bounds, the now 63-year-old Huang, clad in a black leather jacket, traversed the globe as the face of the brand powering the next industrial revolution. Over the past week it all came crashing down. Following two reported extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with an employee — Huang is leaving the company he co-founded 33 years ago in crisis, and thrusting the AI market into chaos. The board is now left to pick a successor for a company that's been run by a singular figure with no second-in-command. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Harvey Jones has been appointed chairman. Nvidia has not responded to multiple requests for comment. "How companies handle a crisis determines their future," former Cisco CEO John Chambers, now a startup investor, told CNBC's " Fast Money " on Wednesday. "How they handle this will determine if they're a great company and a great leadership team beyond one person." It had been a tumultuous stretch for Nvidia, even before the Huang saga led the board to launch an investigation of the CEO's behavior and the potential national security implications. The stock is on pace for its sixth straight weekly drop, which would be the longest losing streak since 2012. That includes a 9% slump last week after the midterm elections resulted in sweeping Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress, and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the buildout of new data centers. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday, and expectations remain high, with analysts projecting 92% year-over-year revenue growth to $109.2 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era. It's a historic level of growth for any business, and particularly notable for a company that spent most of its first few decades as a niche technology provider for video games. Huang founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, he and other executives saw an opportunity to put GPUs to work for computationally intense projects. That technology eventually turned Nvidia into the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. In the process, Huang became the ultimate decider, choosing how, when and where GPUs get allocated. The biggest buyers were the hyperscalers — Amazon, Google , Meta and Microsoft — which needed the chips to build their own AI services and make them available to cloud customers. OpenAI , meanwhile, was snapping up GPUs for its powerful models and consumer apps. To expand his customer base, Huang designated compute capacity to a number of so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius , putting equity into the companies and helping them build big businesses around renting out GPUs. Oracle gobbled up billions of dollars worth of GPUs, going heavily into debt in the process. Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX , did the same to build its Grok model, before eventually starting to rent out excess capacity to Anthropic and Google. Huang wanted the world standardizing on Nvidia. Last year he demanded that Oracle buy additional Nvidia networking hardware if it wanted allocation to its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips, said two people familiar with the deal who asked not to be named because the negotiations were private. In August, Nvidia said it will provide up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio that could be the largest of its kind in the world. "He created the product that started the industry," said Chris Miglino, CEO of neocloud Axe Compute . " Without his leadership we may be many years behind where we are today with AI chip technology, which is the driving force behind the neocloud market." When it comes to investing cash in fledgling startups, Huang is known to host entrepreneurs at Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters. While there could be 30 Nvidia employees in the room for the pitch meeting, only Huang asks questions, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who requested anonymity because they're not authorized to speak publicly about it. One source told CNBC that key aspects of project finance are so reliant on Huang's sign-off that, when he travels, those involved in the deal are forced to wait for his plane to land before learning if they can go forward or if terms have to be renegotiated. Huang's ambitions extended well beyond the U.S. He wanted to be a force in China, which became a difficult market for Nvidia during the Biden administration and was virtually off-limits after Trump implemented strict export controls in his second term. Huang's aggressive pursuit of China may have been his undoing. sources.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
sources.text: A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi. Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out. Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents ), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad : business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.” Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46. Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China . But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.” Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished . The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address. Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing . The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun! Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON , according to Bloomberg . Liang and Super Micro have not been charged. But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists , and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times. The question, of course, is how high this all goes Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point , actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming. More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed , which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “ more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him . The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom . This is what gangster tech regulation looks like. I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested . sources.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
sources.text: The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models. Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion . Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source , whatever happens next. Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology. Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development. Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab. Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem. Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China. The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections. That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons. Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes. Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls. Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed. Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy. As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers. More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs. Huang may be gone, but Nvidia still needs an open AI ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority. TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment. sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Jensen Huang built Nvidia into a $4 trillion AI giant but owned less than 4% of it, leaving him without the super-voting power to protect his CEO role
sources.text: Jensen Huang, the billionaire ex- Nvidia CEO who took the company from a small player in the video game graphics industry to the chipmaker at the center of the AI revolution, once made a surprising revelation: He could be fired at any time. “In a well-governed company, the CEO was always designed to report to the board of directors and the board of directors report to shareholders,” Huang said in a January podcast interview with Jodi Shelton. “If the CEO doesn’t do his job according to 12, 13, 15 board members, however sized the board is, that CEO is let go.” This reality sets Nvidia apart from other Silicon Valley companies, especially those still run by a cofounder. That includes Meta , where CEO and cofounder Mark Zuckerberg wields considerable power over the board due to its dual class share structure. On Thursday, Huang resigned from the company that he cofounded and led over the past 33 years after publicly admitting to being unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into Huang and the possibility he may have been a target of a foreign intelligence operation after reporting by the New York Times explored his close relationship with a businesswoman that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy. Huang reportedly had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him, according to the New York Times . On Thursday, the board appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Still, Huang said in that January interview any future Nvidia CEO would not measure up to him. “There will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company,” he said at the time. Nvidia did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. Despite being the company’s largest individual shareholder, Huang did not have unparalleled voting control over his company or outsized control over the company’s board, like other founders. Huang owned about 870.6 million Nvidia shares, or about 3.58% of the company as of March, according to the company’s 2026 proxy statement. His holdings were far greater than that of other executives and directors, including Kress, who held 4.4 million shares. Vanguard and BlackRock both owned more than 7% of the company each. Because of Nvidia’s one-share-one vote system, Huang’s stake doesn’t come with special privileges, despite his status as a cofounder. That means the number of votes he has directly corresponds with his number of shares. As Huang alluded to in his January podcast interview, Nvidia’s bylaws are written in such a way that the company’s CEO can be removed by the board for any reason and at any time—still, Huang lacked enough voting power to independently elect or remove Nvidia’s directors. While founders with majority voting control, such as Zuckerberg, can effectively determine who sits on their boards, Huang would have needed support from other Nvidia shareholders to do the same. That differs from other companies run by tech founders including Meta, Snap , and even Google. At Meta, a dual class voting structure (it said last month it would add a third non-voting tier next year ) gives Zuckerberg outsized power over voting. Despite owning 13.4% of the company, Zuckerberg controls about 60% of the company’s voting power because his class B shares give him 10 votes each compared to one vote for every class A share. With this voting power, Zuckerberg can effectively elect Meta’s entire board and is the deciding voice on most matters sent to shareholders. Snap, the social media company, has a similar arrangement with CEO and cofounder Evan Spiegel controlling 53% of the company’s voting power while only owning about 9.3% of the company. Even at Google parent company Alphabet , where cofounder Sergey Brin and cofounder and former CEO Larry Page no longer run day-to-day operations, the pair still collectively retain majority voting control of the tech giant. Both still serve on the company’s board. Nvidia’s stock plummeted by as much as 14% Thursday following the announcement of Huang’s departure, before rebounding. It was down about 4.7% as of 1:30 p.m. EST on Thursday. With a nearly $4 trillion market cap, the company makes up about 6% of the S&P 500 and about 10% of the Nasdaq 100 , meaning any reckoning it experiences will trickle through the broader market and everyday Americans’ 401(K) accounts. Huang was key to Nvidia’s operations with a flat management structure and direct involvement in the company’s product strategy and its supplier and customer relationships. In recent months, he has also cultivated a close relationship with President Donald Trump, who has been a vocal proponent of boosting the AI industry and the infrastructure backing it in the U.S.—although Trump was quick to back ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook as Huang’s successor on Thursday. The board has now made changes to its own structure as well. It previously operated without a board chairman, opting instead to rely on lead independent director Stephen Neal to oversee management. On Thursday, it appointed Harvey C. Jones, a former semiconductor company CEO and Nvidia board member since 1993, as its chairman of the board, it said in a statement. Kress, the company’s CFO since 2013, said for her part she is planning to build on Huang’s legacy at Nvidia as interim CEO she said in a Thursday statement. In the January interview, Huang said while he didn’t love his job every day, he always tried his “mightiest” because of two reasons. “One, I’m the best person for the job. I believe that,” he said. “And, two, I have to earn being the best person for that job every day.”

sources.title: Jensen Huang renuncia ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia após admitir traição
sources.text: Por Gabriel Cavalheiro | 12/11/2026 às 11:48 • Atualizado 12/11/2026 às 11:56 O CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, renunciou ao cargo nesta quinta-feira (12) , após admitir publicamente uma relação extraconjugal com a ex-diretora da Megaspeed International e empresária Alice Huang. A executiva é investigada por espionagem a serviço do Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China. A atual CFO da empresa, Colette Kress, foi nomeada CEO interina enquanto o conselho busca por um novo executivo para assumir o cargo. A renúncia de Huang acontece após 33 anos na liderança da Nvidia, que tem vivido um dos seus melhores momentos por liderar o boom da inteligência artificial e fornecer componentes para data centers de IA. No ano passado, a empresa foi a primeira do mundo a ultrapassar os valores de mercado de US$ 4 trilhões e US$ 5 trilhões. A relação extraconjugal entre o ex-CEO da Nvidia e Alice Huang levantou preocupações sobre a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e o mercado de chips de IA . No último domingo (8), o ex-chefão da companhia de chips admitiu a traição em meio a um escândalo de espionagem chinesa . "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações a machucaram, assim como aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz. Sinto muito", escreveu o então CEO. O jornal The New York Times relatou que Jensen Huang estaria envolvido em um segundo caso , desta vez com a vice-presidente de health care da Nvidia e subordinada direta do ex-CEO, Kimberly Powell , segundo cinco funcionários da companhia. As políticas internas da Nvidia orientam os funcionários a “evitar situações em que nossas ações criem conflito”, incluindo “relacionamentos pessoais”. O acúmulo de escândalos envolvendo o ex-presidente fez com que as ações da empresa caíssem 8% nesta quarta-feira (11). A companhia também perdeu US$ 1 trilhão de valor de mercado . Em comunicado enviado à imprensa, o conselho da Nvidia agradeceu as contribuições de Jensen. "A Nvidia é uma das empresas de tecnologia mais impactantes do mundo. O conselho e a empresa agradecem a Jensen por suas contribuições imensuráveis para a companhia e para a indústria", diz a mensagem. A companhia está iniciando uma busca por um Chief Executive Officer permanente e considerará candidatos internos e externos . Até lá, Kress ocupará o cargo de CEO de forma interina. “A força da Nvidia sempre veio de suas pessoas e, junto com nossa equipe de liderança, estou comprometida em construir sobre a base extraordinária que Jensen criou ao longo dos últimos 33 anos”, destacou a executiva. O empresa também anunciou que Harvey C. Jones assumirá a posição de primeiro presidente do conselho. Na próxima terça-feira (17), a Nvidia divulgará seus resultados financeiros referentes ao terceiro trimestre do ano fiscal de 2027. Vale lembrar que, em setembro, a companhia adquiriu a Hugging Face, o que levantou a dúvida se a plataforma continuará com código aberto após a compra.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
sources.text: Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang , no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare. The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role. With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 5% in trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come. “Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.” Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units. The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered the real moat for its business. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.”” Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.” Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 in a San Jose Denny’s and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the behemoth it is today. Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%. sources.title: Jensen Huang Basically Lit More Than $1 Trillion on Fire in Less Than a Month
sources.text: On Thursday morning, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned from the company that had become, in many ways, synonymous with its chief executive. Less than an hour later, when the markets opened, Nvidia’s stock had lost roughly $546 billion in market value. Though it has rebounded somewhat, the last weeks of scandal—including a reported second affair with an Nvidia employee—have tanked the chipmaker’s valuation by more than $1 trillion. Huang’s very public downfall began in late October, when The New York Times reported that the CEO had a “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based chip buyer Megaspeed and an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. (The two are not known to be related.) At that time, Nvidia’s market cap was around $5.2 trillion. On November 8, Nvidia announced it was investigating its CEO, after Jensen publicly acknowledged the affair. By the following morning, roughly $1 trillion had been erased since the scandal started. If you hang out with a certain type of person who thinks of themselves as a daytrader, they might have talked about “buying the dip” over drinks last weekend. If you believe Nvidia can thrive without Huang, there’s still time! The dip has dipped even further. But the early consensus seems to be that this could be more of a prolonged plunge. “Huang is irreplaceable,” Ryan Fedasiuk, a senior fellow at the think tank Foundation for American Innovation, told WIRED last week. “He built Nvidia into the juggernaut it is today, and he was the visionary behind the GPU, which has sustained the intelligence revolution.” There are very real questions about what the end of Huang means for the global economy. Not only are Nvidia’s chips used to train most major AI models, but the company has also invested billions in a number of other tech companies. As of an August regulatory filing , Nvidia owned nearly $30 billion worth of Intel stock and roughly $21 billion of SpaceX stock. For now, Nvidia’s loss is other chipmakers’ gain. AMD shares are up 28 percent over the past five days, and Broadcom is up nearly 16 percent. Nothing to see here. Update 11/12/26 2:50pm ET: This story has been updated to reflect that a third Jensen Huang affair has been reported.
